Purpose This policy defines minimum and maximum stock controls, receiving and reconciliation requirements, purchase approval, variance management and monthly cycle counts. The supplied inventory register contains 2,000 records across four warehouses and five categories. 2. Reorder Thresholds Maintain the minimum stock level established for each product. When available stock reaches or falls below its approved reorder threshold, initiate the purchasing review. The supplied policy does not define a universal numeric threshold, so product-level thresholds should be maintained in the approved inventory master rather than inferred from this report. Before creating a replenishment order, confirm current quantity, recent demand, open purchase orders, warehouse position and the applicable vendor/procurement requirements. 4. Maximum Stock Control Do not exceed the approved maximum stock capacity. Any proposed replenishment that would cause stock to exceed the maximum must be reviewed before ordering. Page 2 Approval is required for inventory orders over $10,000, consistent with the source Inventory Policy. The approval record should identify the product, quantity, estimated cost, reason for purchase, vendor and expected stock position after replenishment. 8. Stock Variance and Reconciliation Investigate differences between physical stock and recorded stock. Reconciliation should identify the product, warehouse, expected quantity, counted quantity, variance, probable cause, corrective action and approver where an adjustment is required. 9. Monthly Cycle Counts Perform cycle counts monthly. Count results must be compared with the inventory register and documented. Material variances should be escalated and corrected only through an authorized adjustment process. 10. Inventory Governance Inventory decisions should balance service requirements with minimum/maximum stock controls. Sales and operational demand data may inform replenishment decisions, but no purchase should bypass the applicable $10,000 inventory approval rule or the vendor/procurement controls.

Page 1 OPERATIONS STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE Rewritten and aligned to the supplied Sales, Vendor and Inventory workbooks 1. Purpose This SOP defines the operating workflow for sales visibility, inventory receiving and reconciliation, vendor coordination, escalation, and emergency restocking. It preserves the source document's focus on receiving, inspection, reconciliation, escalation, and purchasing procedures while making the workflow explicit for the supplied operational data. 2. Operating Data Snapshot The supplied sales file contains 5,000 sales records covering 01 Jan 2025 to 31 Dec 2026, with total recorded revenue of $5,473,536.66. The inventory file contains 2,000 inventory records with recorded inventory cost of $10,019,237.31. These datasets should be treated as the operational evidence used for reconciliation and reporting. Use product/category demand information to inform inventory review and purchasing decisions; do not bypass the inventory policy approval controls. 4. Receiving and Inspection Procedure 1. Match the incoming delivery to the relevant purchasing/vendor documentation. 2. Confirm product ID, product name, category, quantity, unit cost and vendor ID. 3. Inspect received goods for quantity discrepancies, visible damage, quality issues and identification errors. 4. Record the receipt in the inventory register using the appropriate inventory ID, date and warehouse. 5. Hold discrepant or damaged goods from normal stock until the issue is resolved and documented. 5. Inventory Reconciliation 1. Compare physical quantities with the inventory register by product and warehouse. 2. Reconcile differences using receiving records, transfers, sales activity and approved adjustments. 3. Document the cause of each material variance and the corrective action taken. 4. Perform the monthly cycle-count requirement specified in the Inventory Policy.

Escalation and Emergency Restocking Escalate inventory shortages, receiving discrepancies, repeated vendor issues, or unexplained stock variances to the responsible operations/procurement owner. For emergency restocks, document the shortage, affected product, required quantity, business impact, selected vendor and approval before placing the purchase order. Emergency purchasing does not remove the approval and purchasing controls in the Vendor Policy and Inventory Policy. 8. Records and Accountability Maintain auditable records for sales, receipts, inspections, reconciliations, stock adjustments, vendor interactions, approvals and emergency purchases. Any correction must retain the original record and a documented reason for the change.

Page 1 VENDOR MANAGEMENT & PROCUREMENT POLICY Rewritten using the supplied vendor workbook and source policy requirements 1. Purpose and Scope This policy establishes vendor evaluation, quotation, contracting, payment-term, procurement approval, and annual review requirements. The supplied vendor register contains 500 vendors across five operating categories and is the primary reference for vendor records. 2. Vendor Selection and Evaluation 1. Select vendors against the required product/category, commercial terms, service capability and documented rating. 2. Confirm that the vendor exists in the approved vendor register before procurement proceeds. 3. Evaluate vendor performance on an ongoing basis and conduct the required annual vendor review. 4. Record material performance concerns and corrective actions as part of the vendor review process. 5. Contract requirements and procurement approval must be completed before a purchase is finalized. 4. Page 2 Contracts must clearly document scope, pricing, payment terms, responsibilities, applicable service requirements and approval authority. Payment terms in the register include Net 30, Net 45, Net 60 and Prepaid; the applicable term must be confirmed before commitment. 6. Procurement Approval Workflow 1. Identify the operational requirement and requested quantity. 2. Check current inventory and applicable reorder requirements before purchasing. 3. Identify eligible vendors and collect the required quotations where the $5,000 threshold applies. 4. Complete procurement approval and contract checks. 5. Issue the purchase order/approved commitment and retain supporting documentation. 6. Match delivery and invoice information against the approved purchase. 7. Annual Vendor Review At least annually, review vendor rating, delivery/service performance, pricing, contract compliance, payment terms and any documented issues. The review should result in an approved continuation, corrective action, renegotiation, or other documented procurement decision. 8. Control Requirements No procurement record should be approved solely on price. Required quotations, procurement approval, contract requirements and vendor-review evidence must be retained for auditability.
